title: Data-Semantics-Aware Recommendation of Diverse Pivot Tables

statements.text: Given a dataset $D$ over a set of attributes $ A $ and the domain of aggregate functions $ F = \ COUNT , SUM ,$ $ AVG , MIN , MAX \ $, a pivot table takes the following form: $$ SELECT F ( V ) FROM D GROUP BY G $$ where, $ G = \ G_1, G_2, \ A $ is a subset of attributes for grouping; $ V = \ V_1, V_2, \ A $ is a subset of attributes for computing aggregates over; $ G V = $ ensures that no attribute is used for both grouping and aggregation; $ F = \ F_1, F_2, \ $ is a set of aggregate functions where $F_i F $ and $| F | = | V |$; and with slight abuse of notation, $ F ( V )$ denotes $F_1(V_1), F_2(V_2), F_3(V_3) $

bound_sents: Consequently, the problem is NP-hard in the number of candidates, which grows exponentially with the number of data attributes.
This is an instance of the NP-hard Maximum Weight Independent Set (MWIS) problem~ [cite] with complexity $O(| |^ k )$ in the size of the search space ( in our case).
